b: Magnus Carlsen Explains Why He No Longer Misses the World Championship Title!

World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen has opened up about his decision to step away from the Classical World Championship cycle, describing the experience as a “toxic relationship” that he is glad to have left behind.

Speaking in an interview with Total Chess, the five-time World Champion revealed that he seriously considered not playing in almost every World Championship match after his first title defence. Carlsen admitted that he was mainly continuing the journey for others rather than for his own enjoyment.
“I felt that I was doing it mainly for others. I wasn’t enjoying it. And to some extent, I’m glad I had the experience, but I just generally didn’t like it,” Carlsen explained.
He also said that he had been happy playing chess before becoming Classical World Champion and has remained happy since stepping away from the title.

The Norwegian superstar announced in 2022 that he would not defend his title, ending his reign as Classical World Champion, which began in 2013. He won the World Championship five consecutive times before relinquishing the title in 2023.
Despite leaving the World Championship cycle, Carlsen has continued to dominate the chess world and has remained the FIDE World No. 1 in classical chess for more than 15 years.
